originalTitle: Ahead of Market: 10 things that will decide stock market action on Monday
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market has been losing value for five days in a row, mainly because oil prices are high and foreign investors are taking their money out. Even though the market tried to bounce back a bit during the day, overall, investors are still feeling uncertain and nervous. This is also because interest rates in the US are going up and there's a lot of uncertainty around the world. Analysts are watching some important levels to see what happens next to the Nifty, a key stock market index. They're also looking to see how individual stocks and the overall market will react on Monday.

originalTitle: US Fed action, oil swings to test bullion as traders eye West Asia risks: Analysts
simplifiedContent: This is an important week for people who invest in gold and silver because the US Federal Reserve is about to make a decision about interest rates. The price of oil and the current tensions between the US and Iran may also affect the price of gold and silver. Some key economic reports and announcements from central banks will also be released, which could impact the prices of these metals. This means that the prices of gold and silver might go up or down depending on what happens with these factors. The combination of these events will test how strong the market for gold and silver is, and investors are watching closely to see what will happen.

originalTitle: GS, Nomura, Axis hired to run Carlyle’s India automotive platform IPO
simplifiedContent: Carlyle, a big investment company, is planning to sell some of its shares in an Indian car parts business called Highway Roop Precision Technologies. They've hired several banks, including GS, Nomura, and Axis, to help them do this through a process called an Initial Public Offering (IPO). The IPO is expected to raise $500 million and could value the whole company at $2 billion. This matters because it's a way for Carlyle to make money from its investment in the company. By selling shares, Carlyle is giving others a chance to own a part of the company, while also getting a return on its own investment.

originalTitle: Kiwi Will Outpace Euro on Widening Rate Gap, Strategists Say
simplifiedContent: Some experts who study money and markets, called strategists, think the value of New Zealand's dollar (also called the Kiwi) will go up compared to the euro. This means the Kiwi will be stronger than the euro, more so than it has been in over a year. The reason for this is that New Zealand's central bank is expected to raise interest rates faster than the central bank in Europe. This faster increase in interest rates will likely cause the Kiwi to rise in value. As a result, the Kiwi is expected to become the strongest it has been against the euro in over a year.

originalTitle: Wall Street Week Ahead: Fed decision, big tech earnings and Middle East conflict in focus
simplifiedContent: This week, the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) will make an important decision about interest rates. They are likely to keep interest rates the same, between 3.50% and 3.75%. This decision is being closely watched by investors because it can affect the overall economy and the stock market. The Fed's decision, along with upcoming earnings reports from big tech companies, will be a key focus for investors this week. This could lead to some changes in the stock market, so investors are paying close attention to what happens.

originalTitle: CBDT issues crypto asset reporting guidelines for exchanges under Income-tax Act 2025
simplifiedContent: The government's Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) has created rules for companies that trade cryptocurrencies, like Bitcoin, to report information about these transactions. This means that cryptocurrency exchanges will have to share details about the transactions they handle with the tax authorities. The CBDT is doing this under a new law called the Income-tax Act 2025. This change is important because it will help the government keep track of cryptocurrency transactions and make sure people pay the right amount of taxes on them. The international community, including the G20 group of countries, supports this new framework for sharing tax information.
